_meta.indication: ESBRIET is indicated for the treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).
_meta.receipt_date: November 4, 2009 (resubmission constituting complete response received May 23, 2014)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 016 (ASCEND), a 52-week Phase 3 trial, submitted with the NDA resubmission
pivotal_trials.design: Pivotal, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 52 weeks; pirfenidone 2403 mg/day versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 40-80 years with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, DLco 30% and FVC ≥50% and ≤90% predicted
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in percent predicted FVC from baseline to week 52
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in %predicted FVC was -3.7 (pirfenidone) vs -6.6 (placebo), difference 2.9, p<0.001; mean decline in FVC volume -235 mL vs -428 mL (treatment difference 193 mL)

nct_ctgov.title: Efficacy and Safety of Pirfenidone in Patients With Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 004 (Study 2 in the label), a 72-week Phase 3 trial submitted with the initial NDA
pivotal_trials.design: Pivotal, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 72 weeks; pirfenidone 2403 mg/day, pirfenidone 1197 mg/day, versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 40-80 years with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, DLco ≥35% and FVC ≥50% of predicted
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in percent predicted FVC from baseline to week 72
pivotal_trials.n: N=435 (pirfenidone 2403 mg/day n=174, pirfenidone 1197 mg/day n=87, placebo n=174)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in %predicted FVC to week 72 was -8.0 (pirfenidone 2403 mg/day) vs -12.4 (placebo), difference 4.4, p=0.01

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 006 (Study 3 in the label), a 72-week Phase 3 trial submitted with the initial NDA
pivotal_trials.design: Pivotal, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled; 72 weeks; pirfenidone 2403 mg/day versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 40-80 years with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, DLco ≥35% and FVC ≥50% of predicted
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in percent predicted FVC from baseline to week 72
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change in %predicted FVC to week 72 was -9.0 (pirfenidone 2403 mg/day) vs -9.6 (placebo), difference 0.6, p=0.50 (not statistically significant)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) include nausea (36% vs 16% placebo), rash (30% vs 10%), abdominal pain (24% vs 15%), diarrhea (26% vs 20%), fatigue (26% vs 19%), and dyspepsia (19% vs 7%); photosensitivity reactions occurred in 9% vs 1% placebo. Key risks are elevated liver enzymes, photosensitivity/rash, and gastrointestinal disorders.
target_moa: Pirfenidone is a pyridone; its mechanism of action in the treatment of IPF has not been established.

rems.type: No post-marketing risk evaluation and mitigation strategies are recommended.

advisory_committee.vote: A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting was held March 9, 2010 on the original NDA (Studies 004 and 006): split on substantial evidence of efficacy (7 yes, 5 no), safety adequate (9 yes, 3 no), and in favor of approval (9 yes, 3 no). The resubmission with Study 016 was not taken to another PADAC meeting.

summary.text: Pirfenidone, a new molecular entity (pyridone), was granted orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations and received Priority review. Approval followed a first-cycle Complete Response action (May 4, 2010) for insufficient evidence of efficacy; the resubmission (received May 23, 2014) added the confirmatory Phase 3 Study 016, which with Studies 004 and 006 established substantial evidence of efficacy.

citations.quote: Pirfenidone is a new molecular entity of a new class called pyridone, and has been granted orphan drug, fast track, and breakthrough designations.
PDUFA: November 23, 2014Review Priority: PriorityBiometrics Division: Division of Biometrics II
During the first review cycle, the NDA received a Complete Response action (non-approval) due to failure to demonstrate substantial evidence of efficacy.

Positive findings on the primary and key secondary endpoints were replicated in the 3 studies, Study 004, Study 006, and Study 016. Therefore, from a statistical perspective, the overall package provided substantial evidence of pirfenidone's efficacy benefit.
The May 23, 2014, submission constituted a complete response to our May 4, 2010, action letter.

basis.text: Lack of replicated evidence of efficacy: the FVC finding in trial PIPF-004 was not replicated in PIPF-006, and no statistically significant all-cause mortality benefit was demonstrated.

citations.quote: finding of forced vital capacity (FVC) in trial PIPF-004 was not replicated in trial PIPF-006.
The submitted data did not demonstrate a statistically significant benefit in all-cause mortality.
